LESSON: SIGN READING 4.2.1 INTENSIVE SIGN READING: VISUALS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.2: Sign Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Visuals
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Visuals, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to interpret visuals correctly? 2. How do visuals like photos and videos enhance our understanding of a text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Visuals together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: Interacting with digital technology as learner use Google maps in finding directions of places.

● Learning to learn: learning independently as learner interprets visual media appropriately.

Values:
● Unity: Cooperation is developed as the learner works together with peers to discuss and interpret visuals.

● Love: Sharing as the learner appreciates viewing and interpreting visuals collaboratively.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Self-esteem: Effective communication is developed as the learner is able to interpret visuals independently for information and directions in their

daily experiences.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to relate the concept of reading and interpreting visuals with their learning in Kiswahili and Social Studies.

Suggested learning resources:

Course books, charts, pictures, word cards, realia, electronic and digital devices with internet, animated stories with captions or speech bubbles,

cartoons, mimes, pictures, photographs, comics, printed maps.
